visibleText:
Katie Hobbs · Governor

Our records hold who she is, not a log of what she has done: Katie Hobbs is the sitting Governor of Arizona (Democratic) and has filed as a Democrat for Governor in the 2026 election. We have not recorded her actions in office — no vetoes, signed bills, or executive orders are in our files, so we can't give you a 12-month account. The only activity we hold is a set of headlines from her official site (retrieved August 20, 2026), which reference a memorandum of understanding with the Navajo Nation on economic matters, erasing about $1 billion in medical debt for Arizonans, a statement on a final Colorado River item, and a 2026 State of the State address; the site text we captured does not give dates, so we can't confirm which fall in the last year. Her office's own site is the place those announcements are published in full.

question: What does Prop 423 do?
visibleText:

Ask a question about this ballot

Proposition 423: Vail Unified School District budget override continuation

Proposition 423 asks voters in Vail Unified School District No. 20 whether the district may continue to exceed its revenue control limit by no more than 12.5% per fiscal year, starting in fiscal year 2027/2028 and for the following six fiscal years. Per the district's Notice of Election, that would put the budget about $5,102,762 above the alternate budget for 2027/2028, at an estimated continuation of $1.61 per $100 of secondary assessed valuation. The board adopted the resolution calling the election on June 2, 2026, and it is a special election consolidated with the November 3, 2026 general election; arguments for and against were due to the county school superintendent by August 7, 2026. It's a straight yes/no question for voters within the district.

Governor

Four candidates are shown for Governor on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot: Katie Hobbs (Democratic), Andy Biggs (Republican), Risa Lombardo (Green), and Teri Ann Hourihan (listed as No Labels in the general-election listing, though her original filing shows the Arizona Independent Party). Eight people had filed for the July 21, 2026 primary, according to the Secretary of State's filing list: Hobbs; Biggs, Ken Miceli, Scott Neely and David Schweikert (all Republican); Lombardo; and Hourihan and Hugh Lytle (Arizona Independent Party). The primary was canvassed August 6, but the Secretary of State has not yet published its official general-election candidate list, so that final list could differ. Voters choose one, for a four-year term.
